summary: We created and developed an algorythm that predicts Hemoglobin levels in blood during and after space missions. Our project helps doctors and scientists manage astronauts' health and potentially save their lives. The project "UNMASK" aims determining real Hemoglobin levels with their overal quantities. Our project clears the debunking questions related to the previous version of the test kit assay, which is only useful for measuring the concentration.
details:
UNMASK is an interactive research prototype that explores what astronauts’ hemoglobin measurements may conceal. A blood test measures hemoglobin concentration, not its total amount in the body. Changes in plasma and red-cell volume can therefore produce similar readings despite different underlying conditions.

Users enter hemoglobin measurements and mission duration. Our mathematical model compares these inputs against 2,000 simulated physiological scenarios, excludes incompatible scenarios, and visualizes possible hemoglobin trajectories after Earth return. It also explores how additional information could reduce uncertainty.

Our creative contribution is turning an apparently straightforward measurement into an exploration of what remains unknown. The intended impact is to support research into more informative astronaut health monitoring and future mission planning.

We built UNMASK using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Node.js, with Claude Code assisting development and Vercel providing hosting. The model uses differential equations, numerical integration, and scenario sampling.

We considered published spaceflight research, measurement uncertainty, limited access to astronaut data, and accessibility for non-specialists. The demo uses simulated data and is not clinically validated; independent testing against real astronaut measurements is the next step.

Team: Nika Ghambarovi — scientific research; Tato Mtchedlidze — mathematical modeling and product design.
